state_ownership.javascript: Stateless bindings over the process accessibility service, which owns the published tree and a mutex-protected action queue filled by the platform UI thread.
state_ownership.lua: Stateless bindings over the process accessibility service, which owns the published tree and a mutex-protected action queue filled by the platform UI thread.
state_ownership.wasmtime: Stateless host imports over the process accessibility service; trees and actions cross the boundary as JSON in guest memory.

details: Nodes become NSAccessibilityElement children of the window's content view for VoiceOver.
isActive() follows VoiceOver and Switch Control; BUDO_ACCESSIBILITY=1 forces it (for Accessibility Inspector).
Windows and Linux (src/accessibility/accessibility_desktop.c) report isAvailable() == false until UI Automation and AT-SPI bridges exist; update() still succeeds.
Nodes are mirrored as invisible ARIA elements over the canvas.
isActive() is always true because browsers do not report screen readers.

typescript.description: Expose what the app draws to screen readers: publish a flat list of nodes every frame they change, and apply the actions users perform through assistive technology.

operations.name: is_available
operations.typescript_description: Whether this platform exposes accessibility nodes to assistive technology (web, Android, and macOS; not Windows or Linux yet).

operations.name: is_active
operations.typescript_description: Whether a screen reader or other assistive service probably runs (always true on the web, where browsers do not tell). Apps may skip building the tree when false.

operations.name: update
operations.typescript_description: Replace the published tree (at most 512 nodes, in reading order; bounds in physical canvas pixels). Cheap when nothing changed. WebAssembly passes a JSON array of the same objects.

operations.name: take_actions
operations.typescript_description: Return and clear the actions requested through assistive technology since the last call: press, focus, increment, decrement, or setValue (with `value`). WebAssembly receives them as a JSON array.
